sources.citation: Snider, Keith L. 1985. Vowel coalescence across word boundaries in Chumburung. Journal of West African Languages 15(1): 3-13.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress or accent (0 scanned hits). §0 Introduction: at phonological-word junctures 'three phenomena are observed: (a) resyllabification of syllabic nasals, (b) tone fusion, and (c) vowel coalescence.' Fn.1: Banda dialect, spoken in the south-eastern part of Ghana's Northern Region. Fn.2 defines the phonological word as the vowel-harmony span.

sources.citation: Snider, Keith L. 1984. Vowel harmony and the consonant l in Chumburung. Studies in African Linguistics 15(1): 47-57. doi:10.32473/sal.v15i1.107521
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress or accent (a full-text search for stress/accent|accent|prominen = 0 hits). Segmental paper on /l/ and ATR harmony. Fn.3 (p.48) gives only tone-marking conventions: 'The symbols used for tones are: high, low, lowered high (downstepped), falling, and rising'. Cites Price 1975 (IAS Legon, Collected Language Notes 14) as 'an early and tentative phonological analysis of Chumburung' and Hansford 1977 unpublished ms 'The l/r problem in Chumburu'.
